walkthroughs.body_html:
The British Experience of Warfare c1790-1918 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The British Experience of Warfare c1790-1918 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The British Experience of Warfare c1790-1918.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which 1854-56 war exposed major failings in the British army's supply and medical care?
options: The Crimean War
The Boer War
The First World War
The Napoleonic Wars

mcqs.q: What did the Cardwell Reforms abolish?
options: The purchase of officer commissions
The Royal Navy
Conscription
County regiments

mcqs.q: What characterised fighting on the Western Front in WWI?
options: Static trench warfare
Rapid cavalry charges
Naval blockade only
Guerrilla raids

mcqs.q: What did the 1916 Military Service Act introduce?
options: Compulsory conscription
A volunteer-only army
The Territorial Army
The end of the war

mcqs.q: Why did the Crimean War lead to army reform?
options: Disasters in supply, medicine and command, widely reported in the press, showed the army was poorly organised and forced change.
The Crimean War was fought in South Africa.
The Cardwell Reforms created the Royal Air Force.
The Crimean War was a smooth British triumph with no problems.

mcqs.q: Did Britain enter WWI with a fully modern mass army?
options: Britain had a large conscript army ready from the start of WWI.
Britain relied on a small professional force and volunteers in 1914, only introducing conscription in 1916 as casualties mounted.
The Crimean War was fought in South Africa.
Britain never used conscription in WWI.

mcqs.q: Were army reforms like Cardwell's immediately effective?
options: The Crimean War was fought in South Africa.
The Cardwell Reforms created the Royal Air Force.
They modernised structure but weaknesses persisted, as the Boer War later exposed, prompting the further Haldane reforms.
One set of reforms instantly perfected the British army.
